subject: Re: Redwood POC kickoff — scope, metrics & next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood POC kickoff — recap & next steps

Hi Samir / Jill —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned before the kickoff next week. Please reply with any corrections.

High-level pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes on peak traffic for conversational support flows (90th pct latency sometimes > 1.2s).
- Cost per support session is high due to repeated full-context generation; you’d like to reduce token spend ~30%.
- Concern about data controls and auditability for customer transcripts.

Goals for the POC (success criteria):
1) Latency: Reduce 95th pct latency for the support intent pipeline to < 800ms end-to-end.
2) Cost: Demonstrate >=25% reduction in per-session token cost via caching + quantized model variant.
3) Quality: Maintain intent classification and response satisfaction (internal eval score) within 5% of baseline per your eval set.
4) Security: Provide audit logs for inference requests and confirm data-in-transit encryption + KMS key access.

Scope & owner breakdown:
- Redwood to: deploy dedicated POC environment, configure model variant & KV/prefix caching, run baseline vs. optimized workload, provide dashboards and cost/latency reports. Owner: Neha (me).
- Acme to: provide representative prompt set + anonymized transcript samples (see attached sample_data_spec.csv), grant service account access to upload prompt set, and confirm expected traffic profile. Owner: Samir / Jill.

Timeline (proposed):
- Tue 2026-10-06: POC kickoff (1hr) — environment access + SOW sign-off
- Week of 2026-10-06: Data ingestion + baseline run
- Week of 2026-10-13: Optimization (batching/cache/quant) and interim results
- 2026-10-20: Final metrics review & next steps (decision on expansion)

Access/setup steps we’ll need from Acme before kickoff:
1) Create a service account with roles: upload prompt set to our S3 bucket (we’ll share presigned URL), and allow telemetry collection for the POC window.
2) Provide a sample of 500 anonymized transcripts + the canonical prompts (CSV format attached).
3) Confirm compliance point-of-contact for our security questionnaire.

Attachments: acme_sample_data_spec.csv (format + field mapping), redwood-poc-sow-v1.pdf (SOW draft).

Next steps (from Redwood): I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 10/06 10am PT and a DocuSign link for the SOW. Aditya will follow up with the technical access instructions and a minimal IAM policy you can apply.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

—
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood — Reliable, cost-aware LLM inference for production

From: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood POC kickoff — recap & next steps

Thanks Neha — this looks good and matches our notes. A few clarifications / additions from our side:

- Traffic profile: our support system sees ~1,200 sessions/hour during peaks; average session length is ~6 turns, median tokens per session ~450. We’ll provide a sample window of 2,000 transcripts, anonymized.
- Quality metric: we’d like to include a manual human-rated satisfaction score (1–5) on a 200-item eval set as part of the quality check. Can Redwood ingest and run that?
- Security: our InfoSec needs confirmation that telemetry logs will not include PII and that keys stay in our KMS — Aditya, can you confirm the KMS flow?

We’ll attach the sample CSV by EOD tomorrow (10/01). Also happy with Tue 10/06 10am PT.

Samir
VP Product, Acme Cloud
samir@acmecloud.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood POC kickoff — recap & next steps

Thanks Samir — quick answers:

- Human-rated satisfaction: yes, we can ingest a CSV of 200 eval rows (columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_response, human_score). We’ll run blind evals and include inter-rater variance if you provide multiple raters.
- KMS flow: We support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest. For telemetry, logs are stored separately and we can filter PII fields prior to retention; we’ll share the telemetry schema and scrub rules. Next step: I’ll DM you the minimal IAM policy and the presigned S3 upload link for the sample set.

Technical access checklist (summary):
1) Create service account and grant S3 PutObject to the presigned path (we will not request broader access).
2) Whitelist Redwood POC IP range for the telemetry endpoint (we’ll provide IPs).
3) Provide the eval CSV and the 500-sample transcript archive (anonymized).

I’ll join the kickoff and handle the ingestion steps.

—
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood POC kickoff — recap & next steps

Appreciate the quick responses — updated action items and a couple logistics notes below.

Confirmed kickoff: Tue 2026-10-06 10:00am PT (calendar invite sent).
Updated action items: 
- Acme (Samir / Jill): upload anonymized samples + human eval CSV by 2026-10-01 EOD.
- Redwood (Neha): send DocuSign SOW link by 2026-10-01.
- Redwood (Aditya): presigned S3 link + minimal IAM policy + telemetry schema by 2026-10-02.
- Redwood (Rishi): prepare baseline run config and provide expected compute footprint estimate.

Rishi — can you also include the model variants we’ll test (one open LLM float16, one 4-bit quantized variant, and our KV-prefix caching config)? We’ll want that in the kickoff deck.

I’ve attached the SOW draft (redwood-poc-sow-v1.pdf) for review — Samir / Jill, feel free to mark redlines in DocuSign or reply here.

Thanks all — one more ask from Acme: please designate your security POC for the questionnaire so we can expedite InfoSec review.

—
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

From: Jill Thompson <jill.thompson@acme.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood POC kickoff — recap & next steps

Hi Neha / team —

Thanks — we uploaded the anonymized transcripts and eval CSV to the presigned link this morning (file: acme_sample_data_spec.csv) and we signed the SOW via DocuSign (link in HubSpot). Our InfoSec contact is Karen Liu (karen.liu@acme.com).

Quick questions before kickoff:
- For the human eval, we provided two raters per item — will that impact the timeline?
- Any chance of a short pre-kickoff tech sync (15–20min) on Mon 10/05 so we can confirm the IAM and IP whitelist?

We’re excited to get started.

Best,
Jill
Senior Director, Customer Support Operations | Acme Cloud
jill.thompson@acme.com
